episodes.179350: Isolated to scattered strong to severe thunderstorms developed during the early to mid afternoon hours, and shifted south-southwest through the early evening before dissipating. A few of the storms produced hail of penny to quarter sized and gusty to damaging winds, mainly north of the Tennessee River.
episodes.179396: A line of severe thunderstorms moved into SE Texas during the overnight hours of June 3, resulting in several reports of damage from strong wind gusts.
episodes.179398: Strong wind gusts continued in the coastal waters as a line of strong storms advanced offshore during the early morning hours of June 4 after previously causing widespread damage over land.
episodes.179410: Afternoon sea breeze thunderstorms south of a weak cold front across the northern peninsula produced severe hail in near New Tampa in Hillsborough County and a severe wind gust near Wesley Chapel in Pasco County.
episodes.179451: A continued stagnant weather pattern brought a round of thunderstorms during the afternoon and evening hours, with a couple of storms reaching severe levels.
episodes.179453: Excessive rainfall during early June forced a few rivers in the region to go above flood stage.
episodes.179496: Upslope flow and weak surface convergence along a dryline near the Texas/New Mexico state line allowed for scattered thunderstorms to develop late in the afternoon into the evening on the third. Weak mid level winds and a moist atmosphere created a favorable environment for efficient rainfall producing storms. While the storms did produce some large hail and damaging wind gusts, the primary threat from the storms was the intense rainfall rates. Slow moving storms combined with the intense rates to create flash flooding in and around Friona (Parmer County) and Tulia (Swisher County).
episodes.179510: Showers and strong to severe thunderstorms sprouted in the afternoon and evening of June 3rd as a backdoor cold front approached and then pushed across the area. One inch hail fell in the towns of Pennsboro and Middlebourne, and damaging wind gusts resulted in multiple downed trees in the Pennsboro, French Creek, and Rock Cave areas. A tree struck by lightning in Salem fell on power lines. Later in the evening, another tree was struck in Parkersburg and split in two. One intersection in Beckley also flooded due to heavy rain.
episodes.179516: A shortwave that turned into a baggy trough over eastern Texas provided Deep South Texas and the Rio Grande Valley with several rounds of showers and storms June 3rd through June 5th. Large hail fell in a storm just northwest of Rio Grande City on June 3rd before turning into a sub-severe line of showers and storms across the populated Rio Grande Valley. ||Northwesterly flow aloft on the southwestern side of the trough led to several more showers and storms across the eastern half of Deep South Texas and the Rio Grande Valley on June 4th. The storms headed south from Corpus Christi's area and moved along the coast of Kenedy and Willacy Counties before moving southwestward into Cameron County where it produced very large hail, up to 2.5 in diameter, and 80 mph wind gusts at Valley International Airport in Harlingen. Additional storms flared up in Hidalgo County and produced 1 hail. ||The storms on June 5th followed a similar script to June 4th with storms along the coast of Kenedy and Willacy Counties before developing inland. While the storms weren't as strong, they still produced large hail in northern Cameron County and 50 to 60 mph wind gusts near Brownsville.
episodes.179520: Scattered thunderstorms associated with an upper-level low produced localized marginally severe hail and wind gusts over portions of western Maryland and eastern West Virginia.
episodes.179531: Showers and strong to severe thunderstorms sprouted in the afternoon and evening of June 3rd as a backdoor cold front approached and then pushed across the area. In the evening, several trees were blown down in Crooksville to to strong downburst winds accompanying the passing storms. Downed tree limbs and localized street flooding also occurred near Gallipolis.
episodes.179533: Several summertime thunderstorms developed across Middle Tennessee on June 4, 2023. With an abundant amount of instability, many of these thunderstorms grew to be strong to severe. However, with an overall lack of wind shear, they were not able to sustain themselves for very long. Still, several reports of hail and damaging winds were received during the afternoon hours.
episodes.179543: A weak upper level disturbance passed over northern NM helping to invigorate another round of afternoon thunderstorms along and east of the central mountain chain of NM. This isolated to scattered activity covered an area stretching from the east slopes of the Sangre de Cristo Mountains across much of eastern NM. Heavy rains over and near the Hermit's Peak/Calf Canyon burn scar caused flash flooding in the Coyote Creek State Park. Strong to severe storms also produced large hail ranging from Mora County to Roosevelt County.
episodes.179676: A cold front dropped southwestward from New England into Pennsylvania during the late afternoon and evening of June 3, 2023, spawning scattered thunderstorms. SBCAPE was moderately high (>2000 J/kg), and deep layer (0-6 km) shear of 40 kts was supportive of supercells across the eastern half of Pennsylvania. Perhaps the most notable aspects of this event were the large hail and the northeast-southwest cell movement.
episodes.180077: An isolated thunderstorm produced a severe wind gust just west/northwest of Ingomar.
episodes.180266: An area of thunderstorms across central Nye county produced gusty outflow winds.
episodes.180398: An isolated severe thunderstorm occurred as storms peaked during the heat of the late afternoon hours. The storms occurred on the north side of an inverted surface trough that extended from the lower Mississippi Valley to eastern Kentucky.
episodes.180677: Early afternoon thunderstorms moved from east to west over locations near the Mississippi River and westward. While these were intense storms, reports of large hail were less than one inch in diameter in Iowa, but a few storms did produce damaging downburst winds.
episodes.180678: Early afternoon thunderstorms moved from east to west over locations near the Mississippi River and westward. While these were intense storms, reports of large hail were less than one inch in diameter in Iowa, and around 1 inch in diameter in western Illinois.
episodes.180860: Midlevel system provided sufficient lift for isolated severe thunderstorms to produce large hail across eastern Tennessee.
episodes.180959: Scattered afternoon thunderstorms produced strong winds in Washington County and a hail report in Saunders County.
episodes.180975: Thunderstorm complexes originating in the Texas Panhandle reached portions of North and Central Texas during the evening hours of June 1-2. Additional storms formed in the afternoon and evening hours of June 3 along an outflow boundary left over from overnight storms. A few of these storms produced 1 hail.
episodes.180981: Scattered thunderstorms developed over western and central North Dakota during the afternoon and early evening hours. One storm became severe, producing wind gusts of 62 mph at the NDAWN site near Amidon in Slope County.
episodes.180988: A North-South oriented, westward moving, line of thunderstorms triggered off of the East Coast Sea Breeze moved across GA through the afternoon and evening hours. A few storms became strong with gusty winds upwards of 60mph.
episodes.181029: A cool front over east Alabama provided the necessary lift for a few strong to severe thunderstorms to develop in the late afternoon and evening on June 4th.
episodes.181171: Scattered thunderstorms developed across the area with a few storms producing wind damage across Jefferson and Wakulla counties.
episodes.181179: Scattered thunderstorms occurred across the coastal waters, a few of which produced gusty winds in excess of 34 knots.
episodes.181230: A lingering upper-level trough stretching from the Texas Panhandle southeastward into Louisiana and along the northern Gulf coast provided the necessary forcing for isolated severe thunderstorms to develop across parts of North Louisiana late on June 4th. By the mid to late afternoon hours, thunderstorms began to develop in a modestly unstable air mass with the greatest coverage extending from Deep East Texas into portions of North Louisiana. A few thunderstorms reached severe limits with multiple local storm reports of large hail and damaging wind gusts scattered across North Louisiana throughout the late afternoon hours.
episodes.181335: The combination of westerly flow aloft, moderate to strong instability and a dryline resulted in scattered severe thunderstorms across portions of west central Texas. A few the storms were supercell thunderstorms, which merged into a line of thunderstorms while moving east across the area. The severe storms produced large hail and isolated damaging winds.
episodes.181469: Thunderstorms developed along a surface trough in Central Texas and moved across the northern portion of South Central Texas. Some of these storms produced damaging wind gusts and large hail.
episodes.181470: An area of thunderstorms developed along an old outflow boundary over the Southern Edwards Plateau. These storms moved toward the south and produced locally heavy rainfall that led to flash flooding.
episodes.181495: Almost an inch or rain fell around 20 minutes to the east-southeast of Barnum. Minor flooding occurred. No damage was reported.
episodes.181496: A microburst from a thunderstorm caused localized damage to a barn and outbuildings near Lucerne.
episodes.181519: Multiple rounds of thunderstorms the 2nd through the 4th brought high winds, flooding, and some landspout tornadoes to the combined Panhandles. June 2nd brought high winds and flooding to both the Oklahoma and Texas Panhandle. The moisture continued into the 3rd and 4th but with slower moving storms and residual outflow boundaries from the 2nd storms produced heavy long lasting rainfall, as well as landspout tornadoes to the TX Panhandle. One landspout did touch down in Amarillo causing some damage. One of the boundaries that helped produce that landspout also caused storms to linger around Amarillo causing some historic flooding with the city having to pump water out of local playa and storm collection lakes well into July.
episodes.181550: The surface pattern continued to be dominated by high pressure to the east over the Great Lakes region. As was typical in the preceding days, afternoon thunderstorms developed as diurnal heating peaked. On the 4th, however, storms were also aided by a weak boundary moving across the area. Storms developing along this boundary remained below severe criteria, but one did manage to produce nickel sized hail in Ames, IA.
episodes.181925: An upper level storm system moving over the region, combined with a moist airmass, triggered a few late afternoon thunderstorms. One of these storms produced large hail in Mercer County.
episodes.181984: As an MCV moved across the region, strong to severe storms developed through the afternoon hours. Some of the storms produced damaging winds and large hail.
episodes.181985: As an MCV moved across the region, strong to severe storms developed through the afternoon hours. Some of the storms produced damaging winds and large hail.
episodes.181989: An upper level storm system moving over the region, combined with a moist airmass, triggered a few late afternoon severe thunderstorms.
episodes.182150: A large closed low had developed over the northern Great Plains with a weaker shortwave trough to its south. These features helped to initiate afternoon thunderstorms off the higher elevations of west Texas and southeast New Mexico. These strong to severe thunderstorms produced isolated areas of large hail and severe winds as they moved east.
episodes.182292: Scattered thunderstorms developed across western North Carolina during the evening. A couple of the storms produced brief severe weather in the Piedmont.
episodes.182394: A fairly typical summertime regime was in place with abundant Gulf moisture throughout the atmosphere. As the day progressed, sea breeze boundaries became the focal point for thunderstorm initiation and ample instability enhanced intensity of a few storms that resulted in severe wind gusts and hail.
episodes.182686: In the early afternoon of the 4th, a cluster of thunderstorms formed in Northwest Kansas and proceeded westward. While the storms did produce heavy rain, they also produced a single 58 mph gust in Colby.
episodes.182851: Wind damage occurred with severe storms near Encinal.
episodes.183321: Scattered thunderstorms developed across upstate South Carolina during the evening. One of the storms produced brief severe weather in Cherokee County.
episodes.185476: A thunderstorm with heavy rain caused almost an inch of rain to fall within 20 minutes to the east-southeast of Barnum. Minor flooding occurred. No damage was reported.

Damage to a barn and several outbuildings from a strong thunderstorm wind gust at a ranch between Thermopolis and Kirby WY. Estimated wind gust of 50 to 60 mph based on damage. Damage estimated to have occurred around 426 PM MDT June 4 2023 based on radar. Nearest surface observation was a personal weather sensor 4 miles away, which showed a gust to 22 mph at the 445 pm reporting time, but storm did not directly affect this sensor location. Sheds, items, and debris were blown east to west generally with no indication of distinct rotation. Outbuildings had openings to the east, making them especially susceptible to easterly wind gusts. Little to no damage to nearby farms or trees, as the downdraft was from a small storm, leading to very localized damage, likely from an individual downdraft.
